doom.driver: North Korea launches ballistic missile after Seoul demands apology over wounded soldiers.
doom.blurb: THE HERMIT KINGDOM BARES ITS TEETH
doom.summary: Seoul asked for an apology over landmine-wounded soldiers. Pyongyang answered with a ballistic missile, which is what passes for diplomacy on the peninsula. Meanwhile Russia has dropped a second Kyiv bridge in two days, Ethiopia's army is retaking Mekelle, the Houthis hold the Red Sea coast, and an OpenAI safety writer has quit to warn us in The Atlantic, so the background noise is mostly gunfire.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: Agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots are spreading fast enough that Apple is locking down Mac disk access because of the risk they pose.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: The G7 is draining 100 million barrels of reserves under pressure from Washington, ICE is feeding protester photos into Palantir, and a $300M Nvidia smuggling arrest shows export controls leaking.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Russia is striking Kyiv's bridges, North Korea is firing missiles over a DMZ dispute, Tigray is back at war, and Saudi Arabia is reportedly preparing to strike the Houthis.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: The OpenAI employee who wrote the safety reports for every major model release has resigned and is speaking out publicly.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Fault stress near San Andreas is at a 1,000-year high, 40% of health facilities failed a patient-zero drill, and the US military retired an old missile-launch detection program.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — interior scene inside a South Korean military hospital ward near the DMZ, looking out through a wire-reinforced window into the blood-orange dusk, where distant hills are silhouetted in deep black volcanic light; inside, three empty gurneys sit draped in white sheets beside an IV stand catching the amber glow, a wall-mounted television flickers with static-blue light showing a grainy archival missile silhouette, a Korean-language medical chart clipboard hangs crooked on the wall, and a nurse's shadow stretches long across the linoleum floor toward the glowing window frame, the horizon beyond pulsing faintly orange like a smoldering ember under a nearly black sky.

dawn.driver: How AI is helping Mexico detect breast cancer earlier. Mexico is turning to AI to speed up breast cancer detection as long waits and a shortage of specialists hamper screening
dawn.summary: Bridges are falling in Kyiv, Bangkok is underwater, and an OpenAI safety researcher just walked out sounding alarms, so it is fair to ask what AI is actually good for. Mexico has one answer: where specialists are scarce and screening waits run long, algorithms are helping catch breast cancer sooner, when it is most treatable. Add NASA's Roman telescope opening its planet-hunting eye and two critically endangered tiger cubs thriving in Fort Worth, and the day's quieter column starts to look like a real comeback.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: NASA's Roman Space Telescope held rock-steady for its first coronagraph look at the cosmos, while ESA's Juice used Earth as a gravitational slingshot toward Jupiter.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: G7 nations coordinated a 100-million-barrel reserve release to cushion energy price shocks, a sign that collective action is still possible under pressure.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Displaced Palestinians gathered amid Gaza's ruins to play and watch a football match, choosing joy and community in the hardest of places.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Fort Worth Zoo welcomed its first critically endangered Sumatran tiger cubs, and a decade-long deep-reef experiment is revealing hidden ocean life.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: South Africa's Lhuan-dre Pretorius smashed Chris Gayle's T20 record score, a reminder that old limits are made to be broken.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. WIDE AERIAL VIEW looking down at a 45-degree angle over a sunlit Mexican town plaza, vast landscape dominating the frame with tiny figures below: a long line of women snakes from a small clinic door across the cobblestone square, past a fountain and rows of golden-leafed trees, waiting patiently under striped awnings for a mobile mammography van parked at the plaza's edge. The van's side panel glows faintly blue-white from an interior screen visible through its open door, a tiny technician silhouette adjusting equipment. Market stalls with fresh green produce crates line one side of the plaza, vendors and townsfolk glancing toward the clinic queue. A hand-painted pink ribbon banner hangs above the clinic entrance, small but legible from above. Warm golden-yellow daylight washes over terracotta rooftops and green treetops, balanced and confident, with long soft shadows stretching from the waiting line across the stone plaza, conveying patience, hope, and quiet community resolve.
